## What it is

Thirty-one organizations placed across ten workflow stages, from literature
grounding through to clinical and regulatory translation. Twenty-five dated
developments. Sixty linked sources, each tagged with what kind of evidence it
is — a peer-reviewed paper, an independent partner's announcement, a news
report, or the company describing itself.

That last column is the reason to build it. Most market maps cite company
websites and present the result as market intelligence. Here the source class
travels with the claim, so you can see which entries rest on something a third
party checked and which rest on a homepage.

## What it isn't, yet

The map is published **with its own audit**, not without one. The August
snapshot does not currently pass its own certification, and the report says so
in full. In summary:

- **Stage assignments are our coding**, not the companies'. The average entry is
  tagged into almost half the lifecycle, so the stage counts describe a
  vocabulary rather than measuring a market. Do not quote them as findings.
- **32 of 60 sources carry no date**, which makes staleness undetectable.
- **Most sources are organizations describing themselves.** That is the correct
  primary source for *what a product claims to do* and the wrong one for
  *whether it works*.
- **Seven categories have no entry at all** — systematic review and synthesis,
  guideline development, provenance infrastructure, computational
  reproducibility, open-source research agents, post-publication integrity, and
  nutrition. None of those is an empty field; each has real owners who are
  simply missing from this draft.

Publishing that list alongside the map is the point rather than an apology. A
landscape that hides its holes is a monument; one that prints them is an
invitation.

## What changes each month

Each refresh produces a changelog: who was added, who was removed, who quietly
repositioned, and — the one worth watching — whose claim moved from a press
release to an independently verified result.

The map is the artifact. **The changelog is the product.**

## Fix something

Every entry carries a *suggest a correction* link that opens a message naming
that specific organization. If you build in this space and we have described you
wrongly, that is the fastest way to fix it, and corrections get credited in the
following month's changelog.

The same applies to the seven missing categories. If your work belongs on this
map and isn't, say so.
